item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 261121
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Mon Oct 26 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Vance, located a few hundred miles west-southwest of Acapulco,
Mexico, and on Tropical Storm Olana, located several hundred miles
west-southwest of Johnston Atoll.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected over the next 7 days.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Olana are issued under
WMO header WTPA33 KNHC and under AWIPS header HFOTCPCP3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Olana are issued under
WMO header WTPA23 KNHC and under AWIPS header HFOTCMCP3.

$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Public Advisory Number 21
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Mon Oct 26 2026 
102 
WTPZ32 KNHC 261433
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Vance Advisory Number  21
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
900 AM CST Mon Oct 26 2026
 
...VANCE MOVING SLOWLY WEST-NORTHWESTWARD AND LIKELY TO WEAKEN...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 AM CST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.4N 105.7W
ABOUT 265 MI...425 KM SSW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 345 MI...555 KM S OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 295 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...997 MB...29.44 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the southwestern coast of Mexico should monitor the
progress of Vance.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 AM CST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Vance was
located near latitude 15.4 North, longitude 105.7 West. Vance is
moving toward the west-northwest near 7 mph (11 km/h). This motion 
is expected to continue for the next day or so, followed by a turn 
to the northwest on Tuesday and north on Wednesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher
gusts. Gradual weakening is forecast during the next several days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles (205 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 997 mb (29.44 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
RAINFALL: Through Thursday, Vance is expected to produce 2 to 4
inches of rain, with isolated higher totals of 7 inches possible,
across southern Sinaloa, southwest Durango and coastal sections of
Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima and Michoacan.  This rainfall may produce
flooding and mudslides, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Vance,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Vance will affect portions of the coast of
southern, southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few
days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Forecast Discussion Number 21
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Mon Oct 26 2026 
110 
WTPZ42 KNHC 261434
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Vance Discussion Number  21
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
900 AM CST Mon Oct 26 2026
 
Vance is experiencing 15 to 20 kt of west-southwesterly vertical
wind shear.  It appears that the surface center is near the
west-southwest edge of the main convective area.  The latest TAFB
Current Intensity number remains 3.5/55 kt.  Recent objective
intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS have been running in the 45-55 kt
range.  The initial intensity is held at 55 kt for this advisory.

Vance's estimated motion is west-northwestward or 295/6 kt, aided by 
GPMI and AMSR-3 microwave passes from around 0800 UTC.  This slow 
west-northwestward track is expected to continue over the next 24 
hours or so due to a weak mid-level ridge to the north of the 
system.  By Wednesday, a broad mid-level trough near the Baja 
California peninsula should induce a turn toward the north.  The NHC 
track forecast has again been shifted to the west of the previous 
one, but not as far west as the Google DeepMind Ensemble Mean.  The 
official forecast is in good agreement with the latest HFIP 
Corrected Consensus Approach (HCCA).

Although Vance remains in a favorable thermodynamic environment with 
warm water and enough atmospheric moisture, the cyclone is 
experiencing moderate to strong west-southwesterly wind shear.  The 
wind shear is forecast to increase a bit more (to near 25 kt) over 
the next 12 to 24 hours, and this should be enough to cause steady 
weakening over the next day or so.  On Wednesday, as Vance turns 
northward and gets closer to the broad trough over Baja California 
and the subtropical jet, the west-southwesterly vertical wind shear 
increases to over 35 kt, and is forecast to increase further on 
Thursday.  Surprisingly, most of the models hold onto this system as 
a tropical storm for a couple more days.  The NHC forecast is 
slightly lower than the previous forecast, and lies in the middle of 
the guidance envelope through 48 hours, near the HCCA model.  From 
60 hours onward, the NHC intensity forecast is near the lower end of 
the model guidance suite, near the average of the GDMI and HCCA 
models.  It is likely that Vance's convection will be sheared off by 
72 hours, and the new forecast has moved up post-tropical timing to 
this period.  Nearly all of the models show the circulation 
dissipating by day 5, so the NHC forecast shows dissipation by this 
time, just before it reaches the coast of Mexico.

 
Key Messages:

1. Periods of heavy rainfall associated with Vance will impact 
portions of western Mexico during much of this week. This rainfall 
may produce flooding and mudslides across southern Sinaloa, 
southwest Durango and coastal sections of Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima 
and Michoacan, especially in areas along steep terrain.

2. Although the wind threat to southwest Mexico is decreasing as the
forecast track shifts westward away from the coast, interests there
should continue to monitor Vance's progress.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 24H  27/1200Z 16.4N 107.6W   40 KT  45 MPH

120H  31/1200Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen
